Subject: Proposed redlines for Exhibit — key management and controls

Hi team,

Following up on Emma's redlines — I've reviewed the attached PDF and prepared suggested language and implementation notes. High-level options and recommended controls below; I can drop these into the Exhibit and produce a clean v3 for signature.

Summary of proposed commitments (to be reflected in Exhibit B — Key Management Options):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 preferred.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256-GCM for model artifacts and persisted data.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Supported for Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) via:
  * AWS: cross-account AWS KMS key ARN + grant model;
  * Azure: customer-managed keys (BYOK) with keyvault integration;
  * On‑prem: HSM-backed key import (PKCS#11) where feasible.
- Key rotation: Customer-defined rotation cadence; Redwood recommends 90 days and will support automated rewrapping where applicable.
- Key access: Default posture is vendor has no access to customer keys in BYOK mode. For vendor-managed keys, role-based access with MFA and time-bound approvals.
- Key recovery / escrow: We do not retain plaintext escrow copies by default. For customers requiring recovery, we can offer a sealed-escrow process requiring: dual-control approval, NDA amendment, and documented incident justification. This is an exception and will be handled via a separate addendum.
- Deletion & retention: Keys marked for deletion will be scheduled per customer instruction; cryptographic material deletion timeline 30 days after final deletion request unless legal hold applied.
- Logging & audit: All key operations (create, rotate, use, delete) are logged and retained for 12 months; logs are exportable to customer SIEM on request.
- Subprocessors: We'll provide the completed subprocessor list and a 30-day notice period for additions; critical subprocessor changes invoke right to audit/termination remedies for security-critical vendors.
- Cross-border transfers: We will apply SCCs for transfers out of the EEA and combine with technical measures (encryption at rest + BYOK where requested) as documented in Exhibit C (Transfers).

Redline suggestions to the attached Exhibit: I can produce two variants:
1) "Vendor-managed keys" Exhibit — vendor holds wrapped keys; provides operational recovery and monitoring.
2) "BYOK/HSM" Exhibit — customer retains raw key material; vendor receives only wrapped keys or key references; no vendor plaintext access.

Open items for HealthLink legal to confirm:
- Whether BYOK is a hard requirement for Hosted API or only for Private deployment.
- Acceptance of sealed-escrow exception language (we will include strict safeguards).

I will attach TOMs_exhibit_v3.docx with the two variants and inline redlines. If HealthLink is comfortable with the BYOK approach described above, Lauren — we can prepare the execution-ready DPA with Exhibit B and upload to DocuSign.

Regards,

Grace O'Connor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
